title: Procedural geometry (add_mesh) — deferred until a consumer needs it
description:
Deliberately deferred. Recording the shape and the reason so the decision is not re-litigated from scratch.

There is no VertexBuffer/IndexBuffer/RenderableManager path on either side — all geometry is gltfio. That blocks anything generated at runtime: a data plot, a runtime-sized board, generated terrain.

An add_mesh op taking packed vertex/index binaries is contained in principle, but unlike every current op it introduces a new native RESOURCE LIFETIME to manage on the render thread — buffers that must be created, tracked and destroyed independently of the gltfio asset lifecycle. That is materially more work than a material parameter and a new class of leak.

Do this when a real consumer needs it, and let that consumer's shape determine the API. Do not build it speculatively — ship primitives as .glb (mob_scene3d-eih) first and see what is still missing.
design: If it lands: packed binaries over the existing wire (positions/normals/uvs/indices), a mesh registry alongside the entity shadow registry, and explicit destruction tied to entity removal and viewport teardown. Both appliers. Needs scene readback reporting vertex/index counts so the introspection rule is satisfiable.
acceptance_criteria: Not scheduled. Reopen with the forcing consumer named.

title: Ship primitive .glb assets instead of a primitive-geometry op
description:
Cover the cheap 80% of 'basic shapes' with authored assets rather than wire surface.

Entity.data is Model | Camera | Light | Environment | nil, and Model is glTF-only — there is no primitive or mesh kind. Apps that just want a cube, sphere, plane or cylinder currently have to author and ship one themselves.

Shipping a small set of primitives as .glb in priv/ costs zero native work, adds zero wire surface, and rides the asset pipeline that is already validated (glb-only, KTX2, Khronos conformance sweep). It is strictly cheaper than an add_mesh op and covers most of what asks for one.

Take this before considering procedural geometry (mob_scene3d-962).
design:
Candidates: cube, sphere (uv, reasonable tessellation), plane, cylinder. Unit-sized, origin-centred, +Y up, single material slot so the existing material override applies cleanly.

Author once, check in the .glb, run them through mix scene3d.assets validation like any other asset. Reference by a well-known name from priv/ — decide whether that is a bare path or a scene3d: scheme so app assets and shipped primitives cannot collide.

Consider whether these belong in this repo's priv/ (ships to every consumer, small) or a separate optional package. Leaning priv/: they are a few KB and the point is that they are always there.
acceptance_criteria:
- Primitives present in priv/, validator-clean
- Documented in guides/assets.md with the reference syntax
- A test renders one and asserts via scene readback that it loaded
- Material override demonstrably applies to a primitive (tint proves the slot)

title: Material texture override: base_color_texture on the wire
description:
Extend the material override so a texture can be named from Elixir, not only baked into the glTF.

Today Mob.Scene3d.IR.Material carries base_color/metallic/roughness/emissive — four scalar/colour factors. The appliers set them with MaterialInstance::setParameter on baseColorFactor/metallicFactor/roughnessFactor/emissive. Texture providers exist on both platforms but are wired only for asset DECODING at load (image/png, image/jpeg, image/ktx2). There is no path to say 'put this image on that surface' from the BEAM.

This unlocks the 'same mesh, different skin' class — piece colours, team variants, board themes — which authored-only textures cannot express without shipping a separate .glb per variant.

Highest value per line of the options in PLAN.md: it reuses the existing loader, the KTX2 asset pipeline, and the scoped-override mechanism.

Scope: one new field on IR.Material, its wire encoding, both appliers, and the scene readback so an applied texture is visible to introspection. Respects the existing Material.scope semantics (list of overrides with distinct scopes).
design:
Field: base_color_texture (asset ref string, resolved like Model.asset). Null clears the override, matching the existing nil semantics of the other four fields.

iOS: resolve via the existing TextureProvider set on MobScene3dView.mm; setParameter("baseColorMap", texture, sampler) on the MaterialInstance. Note gltfio's ubershader parameter name may differ from baseColorFactor — confirm against uberarchive before assuming.

Android: same shape through com.google.android.filament.Texture and the UbershaderProvider material.

Open question worth settling first: texture lifetime. Unlike the scalar factors, a texture is a native resource that must be created, cached and destroyed on the render thread. Decide whether textures are cached per-viewport keyed by asset ref (simplest, leaks until viewport teardown) or refcounted per material binding.
acceptance_criteria:
- IR.Material accepts base_color_texture; validate/1 rejects non-string, non-nil
- Wire encodes/decodes it; caps advertises the schema bump if the grammar version moves
- Both appliers apply it, and clear it on null
- Mob.Scene3d.scene/1 readback reports the applied texture ref (never echoed intent)
- Unknown/missing texture asset produces an honest error, not a phantom :ok
- Device evidence on iOS and Android: sample_region shows the texture's dominant colour where a tint alone could not produce it
